title: Read a housing ad
goal: Identify the price, rooms and one advantage of an apartment.

objectives.title: Describe housing with sein + an unchanged adjective
Read rooms, area, rent and housing descriptions
Compare an ad with a housing need

cards.title: Describe what the apartment is like
cards.body: An adjective is a describing word, such as quiet or bright. After sein, it keeps its dictionary form: no ending for gender or plural. Use ist for one thing and sind for several. Put nicht before the description to deny it; sehr strengthens it and zu means excessively.

examples.why: Küche is singular, so use ist; hell has no added ending.
Plural Zimmer takes sind; zu makes the size a problem.

cards.title: Turn ad fragments into sentences
cards.body: Ads often omit verbs. First find the room count, square metres and monthly rent. Then make a full sentence with the apartment or room, ist or sind, and a description. In German housing ads, the room count normally counts living and sleeping rooms, with kitchen and bathroom listed separately.

examples.de: Zwei Zimmer, 54 m²: Die Wohnung hat zwei Zimmer.
examples.en: Two rooms, 54 square metres: The apartment has two rooms.
examples.why: The number describes living or sleeping rooms; kitchen and bathroom are separate.
Nicht denies teuer; the adjective stays unchanged.

references.title: Room and ad words
references.note: Read 2 Zi. as two living/sleeping rooms. Read 60 m² as sechzig Quadratmeter, an area rather than a price.

references.title: Descriptions after sein
references.note: Die Küche ist sehr klein: sehr intensifies the size. Die Küche ist zu klein: zu says it is smaller than needed.

references.title: sein: present tense
references.note: Ich bin zufrieden uses bin for I. Die Zimmer sind hell uses sind for a plural subject.

watch: Do not add an adjective ending after sein: Die Küche ist hell, not helle.

practice.prompt: Which sentence means the apartment is too small?
practice.explanation: Zu klein means smaller than needed; sehr klein only describes a high degree.

practice.prompt: Build: The bathroom is not dark.
practice.explanation: Ist follows the subject; nicht comes before dunkel.

practice.prompt: Complete: Die Zimmer ___ hell.
practice.explanation: Zimmer is plural here.
practice.hint: Use the plural form of sein.

blind.prompt: Translate exactly: The kitchen is too small.
blind.explanation: Küche takes ist, and zu klein means too small.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: The bathroom is very bright.
retrieval.explanation: Sehr strengthens hell without changing its ending.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: The rooms are quiet.
retrieval.explanation: Plural rooms take sind.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: The apartment is not expensive.
retrieval.explanation: Nicht denies the description teuer.

reading.title: An ad for Leon
reading.text: Leon sucht eine Wohnung. Er hat maximal 700 Euro für die Miete. Eine Anzeige ist interessant: zwei Zimmer, 52 Quadratmeter, Küche und Bad. Die Miete ist 640 Euro. Die Wohnung ist hell und ruhig. Sie hat aber keinen Balkon.
reading.translation: Leon is looking for an apartment. He has a maximum of 700 euros for rent. One ad is interesting: two rooms, 52 square metres, kitchen and bathroom. The rent is 640 euros. The apartment is bright and quiet. However, it has no balcony.

questions.explanation: The text states Die Miete ist 640 Euro.
Sie hat aber keinen Balkon says it has no balcony.

questions.prompt: How many living/sleeping rooms are advertised?
questions.explanation: Zwei Zimmer is the advertised room count.

listening.title: A viewing appointment
listening.text: Guten Tag, hier ist Anna. Ihre Wohnung ist noch frei? Gut! Hat sie ein Arbeitszimmer? Ja? Prima. Die Miete ist 780 Euro? Das ist leider zu teuer. Ich suche eine Wohnung für maximal 650 Euro.
listening.translation: Hello, this is Anna. Is your apartment still available? Good! Does it have a study? Yes? Great. The rent is 780 euros? Unfortunately, that is too expensive. I am looking for an apartment for a maximum of 650 euros.

questions.explanation: The caller says hier ist Anna.

questions.prompt: Which room does she ask about?
questions.explanation: She asks Hat sie ein Arbeitszimmer?
Anna says 780 Euro is zu teuer; her maximum is 650.

writing.prompt: An ad describes a bright apartment with a small bathroom. Write two sentences: “The apartment is bright. The bathroom is small.”
answers: Die Wohnung ist hell. Das Bad ist klein.
writing.model: Die Wohnung ist hell. Das Bad ist klein.
writing.hint: Use ist in both sentences.
writing.explanation: Both subjects are singular; hell and klein have no endings.

Say that the rooms are too dark.
Ask how much the rent is.

examples.why: Use ist with singular Wohnung.
Wie hoch asks about the amount of rent.

title: Put furniture into a room
goal: Say which room a piece of furniture should go into.

objectives.title: Use in + accusative for a destination
Name furniture, rooms and household appliances
Plan where to put an item

cards.title: A destination answers wohin
cards.body: Wohin means where to, a destination. To say that you put something into a room, use stellen plus the object and in plus the accusative room phrase. Accusative is the form used here for the destination. Der changes to den; das and die stay the same.

examples.de: Ich stelle den Tisch in den Flur.
examples.en: I put the table into the hallway.
examples.why: Flur is masculine: in den marks the destination.

examples.de: Wir stellen das Bett in die Küche.
examples.en: We put the bed into the kitchen.
examples.why: Küche is feminine: in die marks its destination, even if the plan is unusual.

cards.title: Separate the item from its new place
cards.body: Picture an arrow from the furniture to the room. The object says what you move; the in phrase says its new place. In das often becomes ins. This is one word, not two. For plural destinations, use in die. Do not choose the case simply because a verb describes movement.

examples.en: The shelving unit goes into the study.
examples.why: Ins combines in + das; Arbeitszimmer is neuter.

examples.de: Die Bücher kommen in die Regale.
examples.en: The books go into the shelving units.
examples.why: Regale is a plural destination, so use in die.

references.title: Destination with in: complete article set
rows: Der Stuhl kommt in den Flur.
Der Herd kommt in die Küche.
Die Bücher kommen in die Regale.
references.note: Ich stelle die Lampe ins Wohnzimmer: ins names the new room. Die Lampe ist im Wohnzimmer describes an existing location and is taught next.

references.title: Furniture and devices
references.note: A Schrank has storage behind doors; a Regal has open shelves. Geräte are devices; Möbel is a plural collective word for furniture.

terms.meaning: the noun form used for this destination

watch: Ins means in das. Do not use im when the room is the destination.

practice.prompt: The wardrobe goes into the hallway. Choose the destination.
practice.explanation: The destination is masculine accusative: in den Flur.

practice.prompt: Build: The bed goes into the bedroom.
practice.explanation: Ins is in das with neuter Schlafzimmer.

practice.prompt: Complete with one word: in das Bad = ___ Bad
practice.explanation: In + das contracts to ins.

blind.prompt: Say in German: I put the chair into the kitchen.
answers: Ich stelle den Stuhl in die Küche.
blind.explanation: Den Stuhl is the object; in die Küche is the destination.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: The shelving unit goes into the hallway.
answers: Das Regal kommt in den Flur.
retrieval.explanation: In den Flur is masculine accusative destination.

retrieval.prompt: Translate using ins: The washing machine goes into the bathroom.
retrieval.explanation: Bad is neuter; in das becomes ins.

retrieval.prompt: Complete: Die Bücher kommen in ___ Regale.
retrieval.explanation: Plural accusative has die.

reading.text: Mira und Ben planen ihre Wohnung. Der Schreibtisch kommt ins Arbeitszimmer. Das Bett kommt ins Schlafzimmer. Ben stellt den Kühlschrank in die Küche. Mira stellt ein Regal in den Flur. Sie brauchen noch eine Lampe und zwei Stühle für die Küche.

listening.title: Instructions for the helpers
listening.text: Hallo Leon, danke für deine Hilfe! Der Tisch kommt heute in den Flur. Bitte stell die Waschmaschine ins Bad. Der Herd kommt in die Küche. Das Sofa bleibt hier. Wir kaufen morgen noch einen Schrank für das Schlafzimmer.
listening.translation: Hello Leon, thanks for your help! The table goes into the hallway today. Please put the washing machine into the bathroom. The cooker goes into the kitchen. The sofa stays here. Tomorrow we will buy a wardrobe for the bedroom.

questions.explanation: Der Tisch kommt heute in den Flur.

writing.prompt: Your plan: the bed goes into the bedroom and the cooker into the kitchen. Write those two sentences with kommt; use ins for the bedroom.
answers: Das Bett kommt ins Schlafzimmer. Der Herd kommt in die Küche.
writing.model: Das Bett kommt ins Schlafzimmer. Der Herd kommt in die Küche.
writing.hint: Use das Bett and der Herd as subjects.
writing.explanation: The in phrases are destinations: ins Schlafzimmer and in die Küche.

Say the refrigerator goes into the kitchen.

title: Locate every item
goal: Describe where an object is in relation to another object.

objectives.title: Use all nine two-way prepositions for location with dative
Use dem, der, den + plural n and im/am contractions
Answer wo with a precise location

cards.title: An existing location answers wo
cards.body: Wo asks where something is. Nine place words can take two cases; they are called two-way prepositions. For an existing location, all nine take dative. Dative articles are dem for masculine and neuter, der for feminine, and den for plural. Usually add n to the plural noun if it lacks n or s.

examples.de: Die Lampe steht neben dem Bett.
examples.en: The lamp stands next to the bed.
examples.why: Existing location uses dative; das Bett becomes dem Bett.

examples.de: Das Bild hängt zwischen den Fenstern.
examples.en: The picture hangs between the windows.
examples.why: Plural Fenster becomes den Fenstern in dative.

cards.title: Use a map, then choose the noun form
cards.body: First decide the relationship: on, under, beside, behind, in front of, above, between, in, or at a surface. Then ask whether you describe a location or a destination. For a location choose dative, even if someone moves around within that place. Im is in dem; am is an dem.

examples.en: The children play in the living room.
examples.why: The activity happens inside one location; im is in dem.

examples.de: Der Tisch steht an der Wand.
examples.en: The table stands against the wall.
examples.why: An describes contact with a side surface; feminine Wand becomes der Wand.

references.title: All nine: where something is
rows: Das Bild hängt an der Wand.
Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
Der Stuhl steht hinter dem Tisch.
Das Bett steht neben dem Schrank.
Die Lampe hängt über dem Tisch.
Der Teppich liegt unter dem Tisch.
Die Katze sitzt vor dem Sofa.
Das Bett steht zwischen den Schränken.
references.note: Auf dem Tisch means supported by the tabletop. Über dem Tisch means above it without contact. All examples answer wo and therefore use dative.

references.title: Dative articles and contractions
references.note: In dem Zimmer becomes im Zimmer; an dem Fenster becomes am Fenster. Den Regalen already ends in n; den Sofas keeps s and adds no extra n.

references.title: Location verbs
references.note: Das Buch liegt auf dem Bett uses liegen for a flat object. Der Schrank steht im Zimmer uses stehen for an upright item.

terms.meaning: the noun form used after these location prepositions
a preposition whose case depends on location or destination

watch: Movement alone does not require accusative: Wir spielen im Zimmer describes activity within a location.

practice.prompt: Where is the book? Choose the correct location.
practice.explanation: Wo takes dative; masculine Tisch needs dem.

practice.prompt: Build: The lamp stands beside the sofa.
practice.explanation: Neuter Sofa becomes dem Sofa in a location phrase.

practice.prompt: Complete: zwischen den ___ (Fenster, plural)
practice.explanation: Dative plural adds n to Fenster.

answers: Der Teppich liegt unter dem Bett.
blind.explanation: Unter describes an existing location; neuter Bett takes dem.

retrieval.prompt: Complete with the article: Die Lampe steht neben ___ Tür.
retrieval.explanation: Feminine Tür takes der in dative.

retrieval.prompt: Translate using am: The chair stands at the window.
retrieval.explanation: Am combines an + dem.

retrieval.prompt: Complete with the dative plural: Das Bild hängt zwischen den ___. (Schrank)
retrieval.explanation: Plural Schränke gains n after den.

reading.title: A room for guests
reading.text: Das Gästezimmer ist fertig. Das Bett steht zwischen den Fenstern. Neben dem Bett steht eine Lampe. Ein Bild hängt an der Wand über dem Tisch. Unter dem Tisch liegt ein Teppich. Der Schrank steht hinter der Tür. Auf dem Bett liegt ein Buch.

questions.explanation: Der Schrank steht hinter der Tür.
Auf dem Bett liegt ein Buch.

options: On the wall above the table
questions.explanation: An der Wand über dem Tisch locates the picture.

listening.title: Find the keys
listening.text: Ben, ich finde meine Schlüssel nicht. Sind sie auf dem Tisch? Nein, da liegt nur ein Buch. Schau bitte unter dem Sofa. Da sind sie auch nicht. Ach, jetzt sehe ich sie: Sie liegen neben der Kaffeemaschine in der Küche!
listening.translation: Ben, I cannot find my keys. Are they on the table? No, only a book is lying there. Please look under the sofa. They are not there either. Oh, now I see them: they are lying beside the coffee machine in the kitchen!

questions.explanation: Meine Schlüssel are the missing keys.
Da liegt nur ein Buch.
Sie liegen neben der Kaffeemaschine.

writing.prompt: Describe this fixed layout in two sentences: the table stands in the room; the book lies on the table. Use im for “in the room”.
answers: Der Tisch steht im Zimmer. Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
writing.model: Der Tisch steht im Zimmer. Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
writing.hint: Use steht for the table and liegt for the book.
writing.explanation: Both phrases describe locations and use dative.

title: Colors and opinions
goal: Describe a color and give a clear opinion about furniture.

objectives.title: Express liking and dislike with finden and mögen
Name the ten source colors
Distinguish long e from short e

cards.title: Name a color and give your opinion
cards.body: Color words after sein stay unchanged. To give an opinion, use ich finde plus the object and a description, or ich mag plus the object. Finden here means consider or think something is. Nicht denies an opinion. For a masculine object, der changes to den.

examples.de: Der Sessel ist rot. Ich finde den Sessel schön.
examples.en: The armchair is red. I think the armchair is beautiful.
examples.why: Rot follows ist unchanged; den Sessel is the object of finde.

examples.en: I do not like the sofa.
examples.why: Mag expresses liking; nicht denies it.

cards.title: Say what works for you
cards.body: You can soften a negative opinion with nicht besonders: not particularly. Keep color and judgement separate: blue is a color, beautiful is an opinion. In stressed syllables, long e is held with a more closed mouth; short e is brief and more open. Compare stehen and Bett aloud.

examples.de: Ich finde die Lampe nicht besonders schön.
examples.en: I do not find the lamp particularly beautiful.
examples.why: Nicht besonders makes the negative judgement softer.

examples.de: Das Regal steht neben dem Bett.
examples.en: The shelving unit stands beside the bed.
examples.why: The stressed e in steht and neben is long; the e in Bett is short.

references.title: Ten colors
references.note: Das Sofa ist lila: no ending after ist. Die Stühle sind weiß: the same color form follows plural sind.

references.title: Opinion verbs
references.note: Ich finde den Tisch praktisch describes my judgement. Ich mag den Tisch expresses liking without a following adjective.

references.title: Long and short e
rows: eh and ee: long stressed e
references.note: Say sehr slowly and sustain its vowel; h is silent here. Say hell briefly with an open vowel; double l signals a short preceding vowel.

watch: Finding something beautiful uses finde + object + schön; finde alone can instead mean find an object.

practice.prompt: Which opinion is softer?
options: Ich finde die Lampe nicht besonders schön.
practice.explanation: Nicht besonders schön means not particularly beautiful.

practice.prompt: Build: I like the armchair.
practice.explanation: Masculine Sessel is the object, so use den.

practice.prompt: Complete: Der Teppich ist ___ . (green)
practice.explanation: Colors after ist have no added ending.

blind.prompt: Translate: I think the sofa is beautiful.
blind.explanation: Finde + object + adjective expresses an opinion.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: The lamp is yellow.
retrieval.explanation: Gelb stays unchanged after ist.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: I do not like the table.
retrieval.explanation: Den Tisch is the masculine object.

retrieval.prompt: Which word has a short e: Bett or steht? Type the word.
retrieval.explanation: Bett has a short open e; steht has a long e.

reading.title: Two different tastes
reading.text: Anna und Leon kaufen Möbel. Anna findet das Sofa in Blau schön. Leon mag Blau nicht besonders. Er findet den Sessel in Grau praktisch. Der Tisch ist braun und die Lampe ist weiß. Beide mögen den Tisch. Das Sofa kaufen sie heute nicht.
reading.translation: Anna and Leon are buying furniture. Anna thinks the sofa in blue is beautiful. Leon does not particularly like blue. He thinks the grey armchair is practical. The table is brown and the lamp is white. Both like the table. They are not buying the sofa today.

questions.explanation: Anna findet das Sofa in Blau schön.
Die Lampe ist weiß.
Beide mögen den Tisch.

listening.title: A colorful room
listening.text: Mira, dein Zimmer ist wirklich schön! Der Teppich ist grün und das Sofa ist gelb. Das finde ich toll. Nur die Lampe mag ich nicht besonders. Sie ist lila. Eine Lampe in Weiß finde ich hier besser.
listening.translation: Mira, your room is really beautiful! The rug is green and the sofa is yellow. I think that is great. Only the lamp is something I do not particularly like. It is purple. I think a white lamp would be better here.

questions.explanation: Der Teppich ist grün.
Nur die Lampe mag ich nicht besonders.

questions.prompt: Which color does the speaker prefer for the lamp?
questions.explanation: Eine Lampe in Weiß finde ich hier besser.

writing.prompt: Write two sentences: the chair is red; you like the chair. Use Der Stuhl and then Ich mag.
answers: Der Stuhl ist rot. Ich mag den Stuhl.
writing.model: Der Stuhl ist rot. Ich mag den Stuhl.
writing.hint: Stuhl is masculine; its object form is den Stuhl.
writing.explanation: The color stays unchanged, and mögen takes an accusative object.

Give a polite negative opinion about a lamp.
Read Bett, sehr, Teppich, neben aloud.

examples.why: As a color name used as a noun, Grün is capitalized.

examples.en: I do not find the lamp particularly beautiful.
examples.why: This gives a softer negative opinion.

I think the sofa is ugly.

title: Reply to an invitation
goal: Accept or decline an invitation with a useful short message.

objectives.title: Thank, accept or decline and offer to bring something
Build an invitation reply from short fixed phrases

cards.title: Make the reply useful
cards.body: A reply needs a thank you and a clear yes or no. Ich komme gern means I would be happy to come. Ich kann leider nicht kommen means unfortunately I cannot come. A short reason is helpful. With kann or muss, the other verb goes at the end in its basic form.

examples.de: Danke für die Einladung. Ich komme gern.
examples.en: Thanks for the invitation. I would be happy to come.
examples.why: The reply thanks the host and clearly accepts.

examples.de: Ich kann leider nicht kommen. Ich muss arbeiten.
examples.en: Unfortunately I cannot come. I have to work.
examples.why: Kann and muss are the changed verbs; kommen and arbeiten stay at the end.

cards.title: Add one practical detail
cards.body: Treat a reply as four small blocks: greeting, thanks, decision, and closing. If you accept, offer something useful. Mitbringen means bring along: with a normal present sentence, mit moves to the end; with kann, the complete infinitive mitbringen goes at the end. Keep the invitation date consistent.

examples.en: I will bring a salad along.
examples.why: Mitbringen separates: bringe is second and mit closes the sentence.
With kann first in the question, the full infinitive mitbringen closes it.

references.title: Reply blocks
rows: Ich muss arbeiten. / Ich habe keine Zeit.
references.note: Liebe Mira addresses a woman; lieber Ben addresses a man. Ich habe keine Zeit gives a complete reason without an extra verb.

references.title: Bring along: two patterns
references.note: Ich bringe Wasser mit splits the prefix because bringe is the main verb. Ich kann Wasser mitbringen leaves it attached because kann already fills the changed-verb slot.

watch: Do not write Ich kann komme: after kann use the basic form kommen.

practice.prompt: Which reply clearly declines?
practice.explanation: Kann nicht kommen clearly says the person cannot attend.

practice.prompt: Build: I will bring a salad.
practice.explanation: Bringe occupies second position; separable mit goes at the end.

practice.prompt: Complete the thanks: Danke für die ___.
practice.explanation: Einladung means invitation.

blind.prompt: Translate exactly: Unfortunately I cannot come.
blind.explanation: Kann is the changed verb; kommen goes last.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: I will bring a cake.
retrieval.explanation: Mitbringen splits in this statement.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: Can I bring something?
retrieval.explanation: The full infinitive goes at the end after kann.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: I would be happy to come on Saturday.
retrieval.explanation: The message accepts and gives the day.

reading.title: An invitation to a new home
reading.text: Hallo Anna, unsere Wohnung ist fertig! Wir feiern am Freitag ab 18 Uhr. Kommst du? Wir machen Suppe und haben Brot. Du kannst gern einen Salat mitbringen. Die Adresse ist Gartenstraße 12. Wir freuen uns auf dich! Liebe Grüße, Mira und Ben.
reading.translation: Hello Anna, our apartment is ready! We are celebrating on Friday from 6 p.m. Are you coming? We are making soup and have bread. You are welcome to bring a salad. The address is Gartenstraße 12. We look forward to seeing you! Best wishes, Mira and Ben.

questions.explanation: Am Freitag ab 18 Uhr gives day and start time.
Du kannst gern einen Salat mitbringen.
Unsere Wohnung ist fertig introduces the reason.

glossary.en: We look forward to seeing you

listening.title: A voice reply
listening.text: Hallo Ben, vielen Dank für die Einladung. Am Freitag kann ich leider nicht kommen. Ich muss bis neun arbeiten. Am Samstag habe ich Zeit. Können wir dann zusammen Kaffee trinken? Viel Spaß bei der Feier! Liebe Grüße, Leon.
listening.translation: Hello Ben, thank you very much for the invitation. Unfortunately I cannot come on Friday. I have to work until nine. I have time on Saturday. Can we have coffee together then? Have fun at the party! Best wishes, Leon.

questions.explanation: Ich muss bis neun arbeiten is his reason.
Am Samstag habe ich Zeit.
He asks Können wir dann zusammen Kaffee trinken?

writing.prompt: Reply in two sentences: thank the host for the invitation, then say you will bring a salad. Use Danke für and Ich bringe.
answers: Danke für die Einladung. Ich bringe einen Salat mit.

cards.title: Choose a housing type, then a fact

title: Say what you did at work

objectives.title: Build Perfekt with haben and a regular participle

cards.title: Past actions have two verb parts
cards.body: Perfekt is a common spoken past form. It uses a changed helping verb, usually haben, and a past participle at the end. A participle is the action word’s special past form. For regular verbs, put ge before the stem and t after it: lernen becomes gelernt.

examples.why: Habe is second; gelernt is the participle at the end.
Arbeiten forms gearbeitet, with an extra e before t for easier pronunciation.

cards.title: Build the sentence bracket
cards.body: Think of the helping verb and participle as bookends around the details. Only the helping verb changes for the person. The participle stays the same. If a time phrase comes first, the helping verb is still second and the subject follows it. Questions also keep the participle at the end.

examples.de: Gestern haben wir eine Pause gemacht.
examples.why: Gestern fills the first position; haben is second and gemacht closes the bracket.
A yes/no question starts with hast; gearbeitet stays last.

references.title: haben: complete present paradigm
references.note: Ich habe gelernt uses habe for I. Ihr habt gelernt uses habt for you plural; gelernt does not change.

references.title: Regular participles
references.note: Ich habe einen Kurs geplant: planen drops en, adds ge and t. Wir haben gewartet: stems ending in t or d normally need et.

references.title: People and workplaces

title: Choose haben or sein
goal: Report a journey and an activity with the correct Perfekt helper.

objectives.title: Select sein for change of place or state and key exceptions
Distinguish common haben activities from sein events
Use war and hatte for ordinary past states

cards.title: Choose the helper from the action
cards.body: Most verbs use haben. Verbs that describe a change from one place to another commonly use sein: gehen, kommen and fahren. Change of state also commonly takes sein. Learn the helper with the participle. Two important sein exceptions are bleiben, stay, and passieren, happen; neither requires travel.

examples.why: The journey changes location, so fahren takes bin here.
Bleiben takes sein although the place does not change.

cards.title: The person changes the helper, not the participle
cards.body: Use the present forms of sein to make the past journey. The participle stays fixed at the end. An ordinary activity can take haben even if your body moves: tanzen and arbeiten normally use haben. For past descriptions with be or have, German usually prefers war and hatte to bin gewesen and habe gehabt.

examples.why: Dancing as an activity normally takes haben, not automatically sein.

examples.de: Ben war müde und hatte Hunger.
examples.why: War and hatte are common simple past forms for a state.

cards.title: Prepare three notes before you call
cards.body: Write the person, your purpose and the detail you need. Open with a greeting and your name, then use a fixed request. Kann ich bitte mit Anna sprechen? asks to speak to Anna. Können Sie mich verbinden? asks the listener to connect you. Close a phone call with Auf Wiederhören.

cards.title: Stop and repair a detail
cards.body: If a number or word is unclear, say so immediately and ask again. Repeat the detail back before ending the call. Initial h is a breath sound in haben, hören and Hotel. In gehen and sehen, h does not create that breath; it helps signal the long vowel.

cards.title: Read the ad in four small searches
cards.body: Scan a job advertisement for four things: the task, the working time, the pay and the application. A word such as sucht signals who is needed. Pro Stunde means for each hour. A Praktikum is an internship, often a learning placement. Decide which facts match your needs before giving an opinion.

cards.title: Keep fact and opinion in separate sentences
cards.body: A job can be enjoyable and tiring at the same time. Macht Spaß means is fun; anstrengend means demanding or tiring. Verdienen means earn, while bekommen means receive. objectives.title: Sequence a study or work day in present and Perfekt

cards.title: Choose now or completed before you speak
cards.body: A routine uses present forms: ich arbeite. A completed day usually uses Perfekt: ich habe gearbeitet. Start with a time and then give activities in order with zuerst, dann and zum Schluss. These time expressions take the first slot; the conjugated helper still takes the second slot.

examples.why: Zuerst is first, habe is second, ich follows, and gelernt is last.

examples.de: Dann bin ich zur Arbeit gefahren.
examples.why: The journey takes bin; gefahren closes the sentence.

cards.title: Retell from keywords, not a memorized paragraph
cards.body: Write three short notes: activity, place and time. Turn each into one clear sentence, then check its helper and participle. To ask about another day, put was before the helper. Wissen means know a fact; its singular forms are irregular. Use the table when a form is uncertain.

examples.why: Was comes before hast; gemacht remains at the end.

examples.en: I do not know the answer.
examples.why: Ich takes weiß; the table supplies the irregular present forms.

references.title: An order for a short report
rows: Zum Schluss habe ich Musik gehört.
references.note: Danach habe ich gekocht has the helper in slot two. Ich habe danach gekocht starts with the person instead; the helper remains second.

title: Choose this coat or that dress

objectives.title: Use welcher and dieser in nominative and accusative

cards.title: Ask which item; point with this
cards.body: Welcher means which before a noun. Dieser means this and points to a specific item. Their endings follow the noun’s gender and role. Nominative is the subject form. Accusative is the object form after verbs such as nehmen or kaufen. Only masculine singular changes from er to en in these two cases.

examples.de: Welcher Mantel ist schön? Dieser Mantel hier.
examples.en: Which coat is nice? This coat here.
examples.why: Mantel is masculine and the subject: welcher, dieser.
Mantel is now the masculine object: diesen.

cards.title: Check the noun before choosing the ending
cards.body: Recall the article first: der Mantel, das Kleid, die Jacke, die Schuhe. Choose subject or object next. The forms for neuter, feminine and plural stay the same between nominative and accusative. You can say besser, better, to compare preferences without adding an ending after finden.

examples.de: Welches Kleid meinst du? Ich meine dieses Kleid.
examples.en: Which dress do you mean? I mean this dress.
examples.why: Kleid is a neuter object, so welches and dieses both end in es.
Schuhe is plural, so diese is the object form; besser compares preferences.

references.title: welcher / dieser: subject and object

at the market / in the secondhand shop
references.note: A Hose is singular in German: Die Hose ist blau. Schuhe is plural: Die Schuhe sind blau. The gender belongs to the German noun, not its English translation.

terms.meaning: the form for the sentence subject
the form for the direct object here
this; a pointing word with noun endings

title: Say what fits and looks good
goal: Give a compliment and say who likes a garment or needs help.

objectives.title: Use every dative personal pronoun including Ihnen
Use gefallen, passen, stehen, helfen and danken
Give and respond to a clothing compliment

cards.title: The garment is the subject
cards.body: Gefallen means be pleasing to; in English we usually say like. The liked thing is the subject, and the person uses a dative form, such as mir or dir. Passen means fit in size. Stehen means suit or look good on in this clothing context. The verb agrees with the garment, not the person.

examples.why: Jacke is singular, so use gefällt; mir names the person who likes it.
Plural Schuhe takes passen; dir is the dative form for du.

cards.title: Replace the person with the right dative word
cards.body: Use the pronoun table for the person receiving a fit, compliment or help. Ihm replaces er or es; ihr replaces singular she. Ihnen is the polite you and always starts with a capital. Helfen and danken also take a dative person. A compliment can get a simple Danke response.

examples.en: The jumper looks good on her.
examples.why: Ihr refers to one female person; steht agrees with the singular jumper.

examples.de: Kann ich Ihnen helfen? Danke, Sie helfen mir sehr.
examples.en: May I help you? Thank you, you help me a lot.
examples.why: Ihnen is polite you; mir is me after helfen.

references.title: Complete dative personal pronouns
references.note: Die Schuhe gefallen ihnen: they like the shoes. Die Schuhe gefallen Ihnen: you, addressed politely, like the shoes. Capitalization distinguishes the formal address.

references.title: Meaning and agreement
references.note: The noun subject controls the verb: Schuhe gefallen, not gefällt. With helfen, the helper is the subject: Ben hilft mir; the person receiving help is dative.

terms.meaning: a replacement word in dative, such as mir or ihnen
fit in size / suit in appearance

watch: Gefällt depends on a singular subject; gefallen depends on a plural subject, even when the person is mir.

questions.explanation: Grün steht mir gut.

title: Ask for the right size
goal: Request a size and color and discuss a garment with dative welcher and dieser.

objectives.title: Request a color and size, try on and decide
Use the full nominative, accusative and dative forms of welcher and dieser
Describe fit with eng, weit, kurz and lang

cards.title: Ask for a size without changing the clothing word
cards.body: In a shop, use Ich suche plus an item. Größe means size; letters S, M, L and XL are often used. To avoid an adjective ending, request a color with in Blau or in Schwarz. Ask Haben Sie das auch in L? to request another size, then describe the fit.

examples.de: Ich suche eine Jacke in Schwarz.
examples.en: I am looking for a jacket in black.
examples.why: Eine Jacke is the direct object; in Schwarz gives the color as a fixed phrase.

examples.de: Haben Sie die Jacke auch in M?
examples.en: Do you also have the jacket in M?
examples.why: The question requests the same item in another size.

cards.title: Use dative endings after mit and bei
cards.body: Mit, with, and bei, at, take dative. For masculine and neuter use welchem or diesem; feminine uses welcher or dieser; plural uses welchen or diesen. Usually add n to a dative plural noun. This extends the same welcher/dieser system from subjects and objects to dative phrases.

examples.de: Mit welchem Mantel gehst du? Mit diesem Mantel.
examples.en: Which coat are you going in? In this coat.
examples.why: Mit requires masculine dative: welchem and diesem.

examples.de: Bei welchen Schuhen ist der Preis niedrig? Bei diesen Schuhen.
examples.en: For which shoes is the price low? For these shoes.
examples.why: Bei requires plural dative: welchen/diesen; Schuhe becomes Schuhen.

references.title: welcher: every taught case
references.note: Welchen Mantel nimmst du? has an accusative object. Mit welchem Mantel gehst du? has dative after mit; the noun’s masculine gender stays the same.

references.title: dieser: every taught case
references.note: Diese Jacke ist schön uses feminine nominative. Mit dieser Jacke uses feminine dative after mit. The two words have matching endings: welcher/dieser, welchem/diesem, welchen/diesen.

references.title: Fit and purchase frames
rows: May I try it on? (die Jacke)
Sie ist zu eng / zu weit.

Sie ist zu kurz / zu lang.
It is too short / too long.
Haben Sie sie auch in Blau?
Do you also have it in blue?
Tut mir leid, die haben wir nicht.
Sorry, we do not have it.
references.note: Die Jacke ist zu eng reports the fit without adjective endings. Ich nehme sie uses the object pronoun sie for die Jacke; for der Mantel, use ihn.

terms.meaning: put clothing on briefly to check fit
the form required after mit and bei here

listening.translation: Hello. I am looking for a blue dress, size S. One moment, please. Here is a dress in S. It is nice, but unfortunately too short. Do you also have this dress in M? Yes, but only in red. Thank you, then I will not take it.

questions.prompt: What color does the customer want?

Leider zu kurz.
Danke, dann nehme ich es nicht.

cards.title: Listen for the strong beat
cards.body: In ANprobieren the first part takes the stress. In a present statement it comes off and moves to the end. In the past, a separable ordinary verb often puts ge between the prefix and stem. Anprobieren is a special case: probieren ends in -ieren and keeps ge out.

examples.why: EINkaufen splits into kaufe … ein.

examples.de: Gestern habe ich das Hemd bezahlt.
examples.en: Yesterday I paid for the shirt.
examples.why: Bezahlen keeps be- and takes no ge in bezahlt.

examples.de: Heute habe ich das Hemd umgetauscht.

blind.prompt: Say that you exchanged the shoes yesterday. Begin with Gestern and use umtauschen.

reading.title: Two shopping days
reading.text: Am Dienstag hat Ina im Internet eine Mütze bestellt. Sie hat auch eine Jacke im Laden anprobiert. Die Jacke war zu klein. Am Donnerstag ist die Mütze angekommen. Ina hat sie sofort angezogen.
reading.translation: On Tuesday Ina ordered a cap online. She also tried on a jacket in the shop. The jacket was too small. The cap arrived on Thursday. Ina put it on immediately.

questions.explanation: Eine Mütze bestellt identifies the order.

questions.prompt: Why did the jacket cause a problem?
questions.explanation: Zu klein describes its size.
Am Donnerstag marks arrival.

questions.explanation: Stiefel are boots.

questions.prompt: Which item was only tried on?
questions.explanation: Nur anprobiert applies to die rote Jacke.

writing.prompt: Report two actions: I ordered a scarf. I paid online. Use Perfekt with einen Schal and online.

title: Find a department and ask for help

cards.title: Read a directory from the item outwards
cards.body: A directory groups products. If you need a pen, search for Schreibwaren, then read its floor. EG stands for Erdgeschoss, the entrance level. UG is below it. The floor immediately above EG is the first floor. Use im before a numbered floor in a location answer.

examples.why: Ask for the category when the board does not list the individual item.

examples.de: Die Stifte sind im dritten Stock.
examples.en: The pens are on the third floor.
examples.why: Im dritten Stock gives the location; the ordinal ends in -en after im.

cards.title: Keep the conversation going when something is missing
cards.body: First name the item politely. If it is unavailable, ask where else you could try. A reply can name a different department, floor or shop. Check a floor by repeating it with question intonation and thank the person.

examples.en: Excuse me, do you have batteries?
examples.why: Sie addresses the assistant politely; Batterien is the item.

examples.de: Leider nicht. Fragen Sie bitte in der Technikabteilung.
examples.en: Unfortunately not. Please ask in the electronics department.
examples.why: Leider nicht declines; Fragen Sie offers a new place to try.

references.title: Directory shorthand
references.note: Leider nicht declines; Fragen Sie offers a new place to try.

watch: Sie addresses the assistant politely; Batterien is the item.

practice.prompt: Your list says notebooks. Which heading is most useful?
practice.explanation: Paper and pens are stationery.

practice.prompt: Build: The till is on the ground floor.
practice.explanation: Im plus the floor gives a location.

practice.prompt: Complete: Das Café ist im ___ Stock. (second)
practice.explanation: Im takes the ordinal form zweiten here.
practice.hint: A directory groups products. If you need a pen, search for Schreibwaren, then read its floor. EG stands for Erdgeschoss, the entrance level. UG is below it. The floor immediately above EG is the first floor. Use im before a numbered floor in a location answer.

blind.prompt: Ask politely where you can find the lift. Start Entschuldigung, wo and use finden.
answers: Entschuldigung, wo finde ich den Aufzug?
blind.explanation: The question asks for a location and uses the accusative object den Aufzug.

retrieval.prompt: Complete the sign: UG means ___.
retrieval.explanation: The lower level is below the entrance.

retrieval.prompt: Reply: On the first floor. Use Stock.

reading.title: A sign near the entrance
reading.text: Haus Nord: Im Untergeschoss gibt es Lebensmittel. Im Erdgeschoss finden Sie Taschen und die Information. Im ersten Stock sind Sport und Schuhe. Technik und Schreibwaren sind im zweiten Stock. Das Café im dritten Stock öffnet um zehn.
reading.translation: Haus Nord: The basement has groceries. On the ground floor you will find bags and the information desk. Sports and shoes are on the first floor. Electronics and stationery are on the second. The third-floor café opens at ten.

questions.prompt: For a notebook, where do you go?
questions.explanation: Schreibwaren is on floor two.

questions.prompt: Where can you ask for information?
questions.explanation: Information is listed with Taschen.
The final sentence gives the café's hours.

listening.title: The missing camera
listening.text: Entschuldigung, wo finde ich Kameras? Im vierten Stock, aber die Abteilung ist heute geschlossen. Im Fotogeschäft neben der Post können Sie auch fragen. Neben der Post? Genau. Vielen Dank für Ihre Hilfe!
listening.translation: Excuse me, where can I find cameras? On the fourth floor, but the department is closed today. You can also try the camera shop next to the post office. Next to the post office? Exactly. Thank you for your help!

questions.explanation: Kameras means cameras.

Neben der Post supplies the location.

answers: Wo finde ich Schuhe? Danke für Ihre Hilfe.
Wo finde ich Schuhe? Vielen Dank für Ihre Hilfe.

goal: Find and present elementary information about Berlin using a short source text

objectives.title: Find and present elementary information about Berlin using a short source text

cards.title: Pick a source that answers your question
cards.body: A short city guide gives facts such as a district, the place to visit and what to do there. First underline the name, then find the activity. Use es gibt plus a thing to say what exists and in plus the district to say where.

examples.de: In Berlin gibt es viele Museen.
examples.en: There are many museums in Berlin.
examples.why: After the opening place, gibt comes before es.

examples.de: Die Hackeschen Höfe liegen in Mitte.
examples.en: The Hackesche Höfe are in Mitte.
examples.why: The plural name takes liegen. Mitte is a Berlin district.

cards.title: Retell a tip to someone with a different interest

examples.de: Magst du Architektur? Dann besuch die Höfe.

examples.why: The question tests an interest before the recommendation.
Ask this when your source names an attraction but gives no price.

reading.title: Two Berlin tips
reading.text: Lea liest zwei Tipps für Berlin. In Mitte möchte sie die Hackeschen Höfe sehen. Sie interessiert sich für Architektur. Ihr Bruder sucht lieber ein Geschenk. In den Höfen gibt es auch kleine Geschäfte. Die beiden gehen zuerst zusammen dorthin.
reading.translation: Lea reads two tips for Berlin. She wants to see the Hackesche Höfe in Mitte. She is interested in architecture. Her brother would rather find a present. There are also small shops in the courtyards. The two go there together first.

questions.explanation: She is interested in Architektur.
He seeks ein Geschenk.

questions.prompt: Why does one place suit them both?
questions.explanation: The source mentions both architecture and shops.

listening.title: A friend's afternoon
listening.text: Heute Vormittag gehe ich ins Museum. Am Nachmittag suche ich eine Tasche in Kreuzberg. Kommst du mit? Wir treffen uns um drei vor dem Laden. Den Preis für die Tasche kenne ich noch nicht.
listening.translation: This morning I am going to the museum. In the afternoon I am looking for a bag in Kreuzberg. Will you join me? We meet at three in front of the shop. I do not know the price of the bag yet.

questions.explanation: Am Nachmittag introduces the bag.
Um drei means at three.
The speaker does not yet know the price.

writing.prompt: Pass on these facts in two sentences: The shop is in Mitte. There are bags there. Use das Geschäft and Dort gibt es.
answers: Das Geschäft ist in Mitte. Dort gibt es Taschen.
writing.explanation: The first sentence identifies the place, the second its offer.
writing.model: Das Geschäft ist in Mitte. Dort gibt es Taschen.

title: Choose a holiday and pack for it
goal: Suggest a city-tour activity and agree on a simple shared plan

objectives.title: Suggest a city-tour activity and agree on a simple shared plan

Name basic holiday types, travel equipment and sightseeing activities
Recognize German holiday destinations and select simple activities suited to a city, coast or countryside visit

cards.title: Match the bag to the holiday
cards.body: Name an activity before choosing your equipment. Zum Wandern means for hiking; zum Schwimmen means for swimming. A holiday at the sea is Urlaub am Meer. To describe a destination use ans Meer or in die Berge. Use ich möchte plus an infinitive to offer a plan.

examples.en: I would like to travel to the sea.
examples.why: Ans marks the coast as the destination; fahren closes the modal phrase.

examples.de: Zum Wandern nehme ich einen Rucksack mit.
examples.en: I take a backpack for hiking.
examples.why: Zum introduces its purpose; mitnehmen separates around the object.

cards.title: Agree on an activity with a partner
cards.body: Make a specific proposal using Wollen wir …? The other person can agree with Gute Idee or suggest a different activity with lieber. Offer a city tour, a cycle ride by the coast, or a hike in the mountains. Pick equipment that suits the activity.

examples.en: Shall we visit the old town?
examples.why: Wollen wir offers a shared plan rather than asking what one person wants.

examples.de: Gute Idee! Ich nehme die Kamera mit.
examples.en: Good idea! I will bring the camera.
examples.why: The reply agrees, then names one thing needed for the visit.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: I would rather go to the sea. Use fahren.

reading.title: A weekend on the coast
reading.text: Pia fährt mit ihrer Schwester an die Ostsee. Sie wollen am Strand spazieren gehen und eine Radtour machen. Pia packt einen Helm und eine Regenjacke ein. Ein Zelt brauchen sie nicht. Sie schlafen in einer kleinen Pension.
reading.translation: Pia travels to the Baltic Sea with her sister. They want to walk on the beach and go on a bike ride. Pia packs a helmet and a rain jacket. They do not need a tent. They sleep in a small guesthouse.

questions.explanation: An die Ostsee names the destination.

questions.prompt: What equipment suits the bike ride?
questions.explanation: She packs einen Helm.
The last sentence gives their accommodation.

listening.title: A different mountain plan
listening.text: Wir fahren im Sommer in die Berge. Ich möchte wandern. Mein Bruder möchte lieber am See schwimmen. Wir nehmen einen Rucksack und zwei Handtücher mit. Am Sonntag fahren wir mit dem Zug nach Hause.
listening.translation: We go to the mountains in summer. I would like to hike. My brother would rather swim in the lake. We take a backpack and two towels. On Sunday we return home by train.

questions.explanation: Im Sommer gives the season.
He says lieber am See schwimmen.
Mit dem Zug names the train.

writing.prompt: Suggest a bike ride, then say you will bring a helmet. Use Wollen wir eine Radtour machen and mitnehmen.
answers: Wollen wir eine Radtour machen? Ich nehme einen Helm mit.

title: Explain a tram route and a sequence
goal: Suggest a city-tour activity and agree on a simple shared plan

objectives.title: Suggest a city-tour activity and agree on a simple shared plan
Understand and give a short public-transport route including boarding and changing
Order a day's activities using a small set of sequence expressions
Use man with a third-person singular verb to describe general possibilities or a route

cards.title: Explain what anyone can do
cards.body: Man means people generally. It always takes a singular verb: man fährt or man kann. Describe a route for anyone with man plus the third-person verb. Einsteigen means board; umsteigen means change; aussteigen means get off. Each separates in a present statement.

examples.en: You get on at the market square.
examples.why: The stop comes first; steigt precedes man and ein closes the action.

examples.de: Man kann die Linie zwei nehmen.
examples.why: Only kann changes; the full verb nehmen goes at the end.

cards.title: Guide the listener one decision at a time
cards.body: Say where to board, the line, the transfer point and where to get off. Sequence words zuerst, dann, danach and zum Schluss help the listener follow. When one comes first, the changed verb precedes the subject. Use ohne Umsteigen for a direct trip.

examples.why: Zuerst fills the first slot; nimmt stays second.

examples.de: Danach steigt man am Bahnhof um.
examples.en: After that you change at the station.
examples.why: Um means change vehicles here; aus would mean leave one.

references.title: The path from A to B
rows: Get off at the market square.
zuerst → dann → danach → später → zum Schluss
references.note: Um means change vehicles here; aus would mean leave one.

watch: Zuerst fills the first slot; nimmt stays second.

practice.prompt: Which phrase describes a direct connection?
practice.explanation: Ohne Umsteigen means without changing.

practice.prompt: Build: Then you get off at the museum.
practice.explanation: Steigt remains second; aus marks getting off.

practice.prompt: Complete: Man ___ die Straßenbahn nehmen. (can)
practice.explanation: Man is grammatically singular.
practice.hint: Man means people generally. It always takes a singular verb: man fährt or man kann. Describe a route for anyone with man plus the third-person verb. Einsteigen means board; umsteigen means change; aussteigen means get off. Each separates in a present statement.

blind.prompt: Give the direction: First you change at the market square. Start Zuerst and use man.
answers: Zuerst steigt man am Markt um.
blind.explanation: The changed verb comes before man; um completes umsteigen.

retrieval.prompt: Translate: You board here. Use man and einsteigen.
retrieval.explanation: Ein is the particle for boarding.

retrieval.prompt: Complete: Danach ___ man die Linie drei. (take)
retrieval.explanation: Nehmen changes its vowel with man.

retrieval.prompt: Give the last step: Finally we go on foot. Start Zum Schluss.

reading.title: From the hostel to the zoo
reading.text: Vom Hostel geht man zuerst zur Haltestelle Park. Dort nimmt man die Linie drei bis zum Rathaus. Am Rathaus steigt man in den Bus acht um. Nach zwei Haltestellen steigt man am Zoo aus. Der Eingang ist rechts.
reading.translation: From the hostel first walk to the Park stop. There take line three to the town hall. At the town hall change to bus eight. After two stops get off at the zoo. The entrance is on the right.

questions.explanation: Vom Hostel gives the starting point.
Am Rathaus precedes the change.
Bus acht is the new vehicle.

listening.title: Directions for a concert
listening.text: Zum Konzert fährt man mit der Linie fünf. Steigen Sie am Theater ein und am Stadtgarten aus. Sie müssen nicht umsteigen. Gehen Sie dann geradeaus. Die Konzerthalle ist links neben dem Café.
listening.translation: For the concert take line five. Board at the theatre and get off at the city gardens. You do not need to change. Then walk straight ahead. The concert hall is on the left beside the café.

questions.explanation: Am Theater ein marks boarding.
Nicht umsteigen means no change.
Neben dem Café gives the landmark.

writing.prompt: Give two route steps using man: First take the bus. Then get off at the station. Start Zuerst and Dann.
answers: Zuerst nimmt man den Bus. Dann steigt man am Bahnhof aus.
writing.explanation: Both sequencing adverbs put the finite verb before man.
writing.model: Zuerst nimmt man den Bus. Dann steigt man am Bahnhof aus.

I keep man singular.

objectives.title: Write a short holiday postcard with greeting, place, activities and closing

cards.title: Write for the person receiving the card
cards.body: Start with Liebe plus a feminine name or Lieber plus a masculine name. Say where you are, describe one activity, then give a closing. Aus introduces the place greetings come from. You can describe today in the present and yesterday using Perfekt.

examples.de: Liebe Eva, viele Grüße aus Bremen!
examples.why: Liebe suits Eva. Aus gives the source of the greeting.

examples.de: Gestern haben wir den Hafen besucht.
examples.why: Haben plus besucht reports a finished activity.

cards.title: Explain the choice using denn
cards.body: To give a reason, connect two complete clauses with denn and put a comma before it. After denn the second clause keeps ordinary main-clause word order. A location, time or subject can start this new clause. End your card with Bis bald or Liebe Grüße and your signature.

examples.de: Wir gehen ins Café, denn es regnet.
examples.en: We are going to the café because it is raining.
examples.why: In the reason, es is first and regnet second.

examples.de: Der Park gefällt mir, denn hier ist es ruhig.
examples.en: I like the park because it is quiet here.
examples.why: Hier is first after denn; ist comes before es.

reading.translation: Dear Paul, we are in Cologne. Yesterday we visited the cathedral. Today we are travelling by boat because the sun is shining. Tomorrow we will buy a present for grandma. See you soon and best wishes, Nina.
